editorial.headline: The Water Systems Inside KBLI 43221
editorial.standfirst: A plumbing activity spanning clean water, wastewater, drainage and sanitary installations is nationally open to full foreign ownership and remains available for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
Plumbing is the building’s water-and-waste system, and KBLI 43221 covers its installation, repair and maintenance. Its scope is concrete: clean-water, wastewater and drainage lines, together with sanitary equipment, in both residential and non-residential buildings. It also includes water piping, clean-water distribution pipes, wastewater pipes, and the installation of water-treatment plant or reverse-osmosis installations. The activity is defined by the physical systems that bring water in, move it through a building and take wastewater away.

The registration field is open at every recorded scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That breadth reflects the settings stated in the scope, from housing to non-residential buildings, and the defined work across piping, drainage, sanitary equipment and treatment installations. The record identifies the plumbing-installation sub-classification as IN007. The decisive question is the work itself: installation, repair or maintenance of the specified clean-water, wastewater and drainage systems.

Nationally, the PMA position is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. The national reading is therefore direct: a foreign-owned business may use this activity at the recorded national ceiling. Bali’s position also needs to be read directly against the provincial rule. The province permanently blocks PMA registration for low- and medium-low-risk activities, island-wide. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium. The Bali record explains why: at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi—medium-high/high—rather than a risk band caught by the moratorium.

In Bali, a foreign-owned company may register this activity today: it carries the Bali status OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and is not caught by the permanent PMA moratorium. The record states no further Bali-side ownership figure or partnership condition. The national ceiling remains 100%, while the Bali finding is a no-block outcome rooted in the reported large-scale OSS risk. For this plumbing activity, the national and Bali positions align clearly: it is open nationally and available for PMA registration in Bali.
